## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Blind review. The guidelines refer to the "integrity of the blind review process", ask for a separate title page with all authors' contact details, warn that excessive self-citation can compromise anonymity, and ask authors to remove working papers from public websites before submitting (guidelines, Wayback copy of 2025-07-11, https://web.archive.org/web/20250711084530/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/ASQ ). Whether review is single- or double-blind is not worded on the pages read; the separate title page and the self-citation warning suggest authors are blinded to reviewers (inference). Three reviewers is the norm but not guaranteed; the handling editor may also use only one or two reviewers with particular expertise. The editor decides only on manuscripts the editor handles; each associate editor makes their own decisions and may differ from the reviewers' recommendations (FAQ for authors, file stamp 2024-04-03) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No transfer policy found on the pages read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No statement found |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Not given as a number. The FAQ says some manuscripts are accepted after the first revision but most are not, and others go through two or more rounds; the revision deadline is set to one year in the submission system by default (FAQ for authors) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Authors may suggest reviewers in the cover letter (the submission system no longer allows listing them in a field); suggestions must have no conflicts and the editors need not follow them (guidelines, Wayback copy of 2025-07-11). Authors may request a handling editor; the editor considers requests but assigns case by case (FAQ) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Partly. The guidelines (Wayback copy of 2025-07-11) say that if AI-powered tools are used in manuscript preparation, the submitting author is fully responsible for accuracy, presentation and appropriate citation of other scholars' work, and point to the Sage AI policy. The detailed rules are the publisher-wide Sage policy |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Sage policy (the live page https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/artificial-intelligence-policy returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-23, 5 tries; the text was read on the Wayback copy dated 2026-11-05, https://web.archive.org/web/20261105171425id_/https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/artificial-intelligence-policy, which sorts AI use as "assistive (and no longer requiring disclosure), generative (requiring disclosure), and prohibitive"): assistive use such as language, grammar or structure suggestions needs no disclosure; generative use that produces content affecting methodology, analysis, results or conclusions must be disclosed on submission |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed; generative use needs disclosure, assistive use does not; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | Sage policy: disclosure required for generative uses such as literature compilation, translation, AI-generated code, visualisation, illustrations and reference compilation; authors verify all outputs and cite original sources rather than AI tools as primary sources; inappropriate use includes fabricated references, generated data, and AI interviews in place of participants; an editor who finds undisclosed inappropriate use can reject at any stage; reviewers may use AI to help write and format their reports but stay responsible, and must not breach confidentiality; editors must not use AI to generate decision letters or summaries of unpublished research |
| **Source URL** | https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/artificial-intelligence-policy ; https://web.archive.org/web/20250711084530/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/ASQ |

## Format

> Sources: guidelines (Wayback copy of 2025-07-11) and the journal's formatting-guidelines and FAQ PDFs listed under Identity, read 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research papers, theory papers and book reviews. The guidelines say theory-only papers and papers focused mainly on empirics or problems are considered, but that the combination of theory and empirical evidence generally offers the strongest contribution and that theory-only or empirics-only papers "have less often succeeded" (paraphrase; Wayback copy of 2025-07-11). OpenAlex types of the 291 records dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23: 138 articles, 140 book reviews, 11 editorials; the board lists two Book Review Editors, so reviews are an editor-run route (inference) |
| **Word limit** | No page limit is published. Suggested length 35 to 45 pages of text (12 point Times New Roman, double spaced, 1-inch margins) plus references, tables, figures and appendices; editors will unsubmit a very long manuscript and request cuts. The FAQ says quantitative papers with over 40 text pages and qualitative or mixed-methods papers over 50 draw more scrutiny, and any first submission over 60 pages total attracts attention |
| **Word limit negotiability** | The FAQ treats length relative to contribution as the test: a long paper with a clear substantial contribution may fare better than a shorter paper with a minor one (FAQ, file stamp 2024-04-03). No formal exception rule |
| **Abstract limit** | 200 words or fewer, informative, avoiding jargon (guidelines, Wayback copy of 2025-07-11). Keywords chosen from the ASQ topic and methods lists in the submission system; the FAQ says the handling editor may use them to find reviewers |
| **Reference limit** | No cap found. Since January 2025 the journal follows APA style for in-text citations and references; for first submissions and revisions another reference format is acceptable if sources are identifiable, and APA format is required after provisional acceptance (guidelines; formatting guidelines PDF) |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplemental material may be placed online in anonymised form and linked in the manuscript to save space; the FAQ warns that some reviewers may not visit it, so core material belongs in the paper or an appendix |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. For a first submission figures and tables may be embedded or placed at the end; accepted papers need them grouped after the references, tables in editable form; figures print in greyscale (formatting guidelines PDF) |
| **Style / submission format** | Word or PDF at submission, Word required for accepted papers; double-spaced 12 point Times New Roman; footnotes used sparingly; three heading levels, unnumbered; separate title page; cover letter that lists people who have seen the paper, thesis-committee members and conflicted colleagues, and states any overlap with other papers (guidelines; formatting guidelines PDF). Submitted through ScholarOne (https://mc.manuscriptcentral.com/asq per the guidelines) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Three editorial criteria are stated: advance understanding of organizing in contexts such as teams, enterprises or markets; develop a new theoretical account or empirical findings that challenge earlier understandings; address a significant and challenging management problem (paraphrase; guidelines, Wayback copy of 2025-07-11, https://web.archive.org/web/20250711084530/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/ASQ ).
- **What kind of engagement?** Grounding in some organizational literature, conversation or insight is required, and a lack of theoretical grounding is not welcome; the editors ask "What's interesting here?" while warning against novelty as a substitute for insight (paraphrase; same page). A single key point stated in one sentence is expected (https://web.archive.org/web/20250711084530/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/ASQ ).
- **Article type and length**: suggested 35 to 45 pages of text plus references and tables, abstract 200 words or fewer, keywords from the submission-system list (guidelines https://web.archive.org/web/20250711084530/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/ASQ ; FAQ http://journals.sagepub.com/pb-assets/cmscontent/ASQ/6.%20FAQs%20for%20ASQ%20Authors-1712174957.pdf ).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: none found on the pages read.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: manuscripts judged inappropriate "will be returned promptly" (guidelines, Wayback copy of 2025-07-11); about one-half of new submissions are desk rejected for suitability or fit (FAQ for authors, http://journals.sagepub.com/pb-assets/cmscontent/ASQ/6.%20FAQs%20for%20ASQ%20Authors-1712174957.pdf , file stamp 2024-04-03). A rejected paper cannot be reworked and resubmitted unless the decision letter explicitly allows it, which the FAQ says is rarely offered (same FAQ).


### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are articles of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex: 138 records of type article, 120 with an abstract) whose title or abstract matches the regex in the keyword table (AI-Research Notes); shares use the 120 abstract records as denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none gives a preference for one method (the guidelines say no methodological style is given greater significance). Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | Survey, questionnaire, experiment or quantitative terms 22 of 120 (18.3%); regression, panel, archival or longitudinal terms 16 (13.3%). Guidelines: data from archives, the lab or the field are accepted (Wayback copy of 2025-07-11) |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | "interview" 15 (12.5%), "qualitative" 18 (15.0%) of 120. The journal's transparency policy gives separate expectations for qualitative data, and the FAQ points to an editorial essay on transparency in qualitative work |
| Autoethnography | 0 | "autoethnograph" 0 of 120 |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | "theoretical" 15 (12.5%), "conceptual" 9 (7.5%) of 120. Guidelines: theory-only papers are considered but have less often succeeded in review |
| Mixed methods | 2 | "mixed methods" 2 of 120 (1.7%); the Cornell page lists multi-method work among welcomed approaches |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 1 | "meta-analysis" 1 of 120 (0.8%); "systematic review" 0 |
| Ethnography and case study (added row) | 3 | ethnograph- 12 (10.0%) and "case study" 5 (4.2%) of 120 |
| Simulation / formal model (added row) | 0 | 0 of 120 abstract records, although the Cornell page and guidelines name simulations and formal models among accepted approaches (count rule gives 0; the statement is recorded here and not used to raise the score) |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Not found in the journal's own pages. The data and methods transparency policy expects interview studies to include an interview protocol and an anonymised description or table of interviewees, and recognises that ethical or legal considerations may prohibit sharing data (https://journals.sagepub.com/pb-assets/cmscontent/ASQ/Data%20and%20Methods%20Transparency%20Policy%20040324-1712174442.pdf, read 2026-11-23). The Sage research ethics policy for humanities and social sciences could not be read (see AI-Research Notes) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers appear: 36 of 121 article records with author data (29.8%; OpenAlex, retrieved 2026-11-23). The guidelines say "we" is for multiple authors only (Wayback copy of 2025-07-11) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Sage states it welcomes submissions from independent researchers, does not discriminate by affiliation status, and may ask for underlying data, funding documentation or ethics approvals (https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/policy-on-submissions-from-independent-researchers, read 2026-11-23). ASQ asks that each author's affiliation be where the research was conducted (guidelines, Wayback copy of 2025-07-11) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Required: all authors must explain how they will share information on their data and methods in a way suited to their data and methods, and the plan must be implemented before acceptance (Data and Methods Transparency Policy PDF above; guidelines, Wayback copy of 2025-07-11). Sage's general data policy is at https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/research-data-sharing-policies |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Blind review with a separate title page; authors should take precautions to preserve blinding, remove working papers from public websites where possible, and avoid excessive self-citation (guidelines). The cover letter must list people who have seen the paper and any overlapping submissions (same page) |
| **AI use** | Submitting author fully responsible; Sage policy requires disclosure of generative uses (https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/artificial-intelligence-policy) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid evidence in OpenAlex (62 of 138 articles); APC amount not found (see Open Access) |
| **Prior publication and resubmission** | A paper under review elsewhere cannot be submitted; related papers must be disclosed; a rejected manuscript should not be resubmitted, even revised, unless the decision letter explicitly invites it (guidelines, Wayback copy of 2025-07-11; FAQ PDF). ASQ cannot give pre-review feedback, including on fit (FAQ PDF) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Transparency plan**: all authors must explain how they will share data and methods information and implement the plan before acceptance (Practical Concerns, transparency policy PDF).
- **Concurrent submission and prior rejection**: a paper under review elsewhere cannot be submitted; a manuscript ASQ rejected should not be resubmitted unless the decision letter invites it (Practical Concerns, guidelines and FAQ).
- **Scope and grounding**: manuscripts without grounding in an organizational literature or conversation are described as inappropriate and returned promptly (Framing Requirements).
- **Length**: very long manuscripts are unsubmitted and returned for cuts (Format).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read.

### Soft Tax

- **Selectivity**: the journal states about one-half of new submissions are desk rejected and acceptance has been about 5 percent of new submissions in recent years (Metrics, FAQ). These are journal-stated figures; their year is not printed.
- **Time**: the stated goal is a decision in 60 to 90 days once a paper goes out for review; revision deadlines default to one year (Review Cycle Time).
- **Preprint**: authors are asked to remove public working papers before submitting (Preprint Policy).
- **Reference style**: APA after provisional acceptance (Format).
- **Length per page**: suggested 35 to 45 text pages; the contribution-to-length ratio is judged (Format).

### Best Suited For

- Papers combining a theoretical contribution with qualitative or quantitative empirical evidence on organizing: the guidelines say that combination is strongest; interview, qualitative, survey or experiment terms each appear in 12 to 18 percent of abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Ethnographic or archival work: ethnograph- 10.0%, regression/archival/panel 13.3% of abstracts (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Work on inequality, gender, race, identity and algorithmic management: counts of 10 to 16 percent for inequality, gender, race and identity, and algorithmic management among the most cited (Sensitive Topics, Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Concise, single-argument writing in active voice with first person: the guidelines and 117 of 120 abstracts (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Theory-only papers: the guidelines say they are considered but less often succeed (Format; Methodological Preferences).
- Formal-model or simulation papers if a precedent in the journal is needed: 0 of 120 abstract records match, although the journal lists them as welcome (Methodological Preferences).
- Authors needing a verified turnaround figure: only a stated goal and one SciRev entry exist (Review Cycle Time).
- Work centred on decolonial, Indigenous or non-Western framing as the main contribution: 0 of 120 abstracts match (Sensitive Topics); this shows absence in the window, not a stated policy.
